title: Quantum Computers vs Quantum Simulators
prerequisites: Topic 1.3 (noisy vs fault-tolerant devices; what "quantum advantage" means)
summary: This topic explains the difference between a real quantum computer (a physical device) and a quantum simulator (a classical program that calculates what a quantum circuit would do). Learners see how a simulator works, why its cost doubles with every added qubit, what a simulator can show that hardware cannot, why hardware results differ from ideal results, and when each tool should be used.
learning_objectives: Explain the difference between a quantum computer and a quantum simulator, including what hardware each runs on.
Describe how a state-vector simulator applies gates and produces measurement probabilities, and carry out a two-qubit example by hand.
Calculate the memory needed to store an n-qubit state vector and explain why simulation does not scale to large general circuits.
Distinguish exact probabilities from sampled shot counts, and estimate the statistical uncertainty of a shot-based estimate.
List at least three reasons why a circuit's results on real hardware can differ from its ideal simulation.

Identify circuit families that can be simulated efficiently on a classical computer (Clifford circuits, low entanglement) and explain why this does not contradict the difficulty of general simulation.
Decide whether a simulator or real hardware is the right tool for a given task, and avoid confusing "quantum simulator" with "quantum simulation" of physical systems.
verification_note: Numerical/circuit results are source-derived and must be confirmed in the project simulator/calculator before release.
time_sensitivity: 1.4 intentionally avoids vendor-specific current hardware numbers; simulator facts and circuit results still require project-simulator verification.

conventions.qiskit_display: Qiskit-style tools may print the reverse order (q1 q0); tutor should state the ordering used.
